papers.title: pinn-serving: Derivative-Aware Serving of Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: A serving harness and benchmark suite for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). Introduces derivative-graph baking, which differentiates a tanh MLP symbolically offline and emits the closed-form derivative recursion as a forward-only program, making derivative-valued queries compatible with standard inference backends and quantisation. Includes evidence that output-space accuracy monitoring cannot detect physics degradation at serving time, and a matched comparison against a Crank-Nicolson solver.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Approach to Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: Abstract Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have become a revolutionary computational paradigm that combines the power of data-driven learning with the laws of physics to solve forward and inverse problems of partial differential equations (PDEs). Formally introduced by Raissi et al., PINNs substitute the residue of a PDE, along with the initial and boundary conditions, into the loss function of a neural network, which computes the necessary derivatives through automatic differentiation. Unlike classical numerical solvers, like the finite element method or finite difference method, PINNs are mesh-less, easy to adapt to irregular geometries, can treat high dimensional problems naturally, and provide a natural framework to integrate sparse observational information with the underlying physical model. This review summarizes the mathematical background of PINNs, architectures and training approaches to address their limitations, and the key variants, such as extended PINNs (XPINNs), conservative PINNs (cPINNs), and operator-learning frameworks like DeepONet (Deep Learning Operator Network), and Fourier neural operators. A survey of applications in fluid mechanics, heat transfer, solid mechanics, biomedical modeling and geophysics is conducted. The continued difficulties with training stability, spectral bias, multi-scale problem and theoretical convergence guarantees are discussed and future prospects for adaptive sampling, causal training and hybrid solver–network schemes are highlighted.

papers.title: Direct Anterior Approach is Associated with Superior Postoperative Sexual Function Compared with Anterolateral Approach in Men Undergoing Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Prospective Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is increasingly performed in younger men, many of whom regard sexual function as an important component of postoperative quality of life. Regular sexual activity contributes to overall well-being. Hip osteoarthritis (OA) impairs sexual activity in up to 70% of patients, and THA may restore it and improve sexual quality of life. Although the direct anterior approach (DAA) has been associated with faster recovery, its influence on patient-centred outcomes such as sexual health remains insufficiently studied. To our knowledge, erectile function after THA has not been compared between surgical approaches. Methods In this prospective multicentre cohort study, 87 sexually active men aged 18–65 years underwent primary THA via either DAA ( n = 49) or the anterolateral approach (ALA; n = 38). Outcomes were assessed preoperatively and 6 months postoperatively using the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC; pain, stiffness, function), the World Health Organization Quality of Life-BREF (WHOQOL-BREF; physical and psychological domains), and the International Index of Erectile Function-5 (IIEF-5). Data were analysed using two-way mixed-design ANOVAs. Results Both groups demonstrated significant postoperative improvements in pain, stiffness, physical function, and quality of life. Compared with the ALA group, the DAA group had lower postoperative pain and greater reduction in stiffness (both p < .001). Erectile function improved significantly in the DAA group ( p < .001), whereas no significant change was observed in the ALA group. Conversely, the ALA group showed greater improvements in physical well-being ( p = .049) and psychological well-being ( p < .001). Conclusions Both approaches improved function and quality of life after THA. DAA was associated with greater reductions in pain and stiffness and may confer an additional benefit in erectile function, whereas ALA was associated with greater perceived gains in overall well-being. Larger studies with more comparable cohorts are warranted.

papers.title: Management of Pain, Mobilization, and Pressure Injuries in Complex Revision Arthroplasty: A Multidisciplinary Case Report
papers.abstract: Complex revision arthroplasties are indicated particularly in cases of severe bone loss, aseptic loosening, periprosthetic infection, and recurrent instability. Revision total hip arthroplasty is associated with higher complication rates and greater functional limitations than primary surgery. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of a multidisciplinary approach on pain, mobilization, and pressure injury following revision hip arthroplasty in a high-risk patient. The case involved a 75-year-old patient with a history of multiple partial hip arthroplasties and revision procedures. Preoperative assessment revealed acetabular protrusion and femoral and pelvic bone defects. Pelvic reconstruction was performed using an ilioischial cage, a distally fixed femoral stem, and a constrained liner to address instability. Postoperative care was provided by a multidisciplinary team consisting of orthopedic surgeons, an orthopedic nurse, and a physiotherapist. Management included hemodynamic stabilization, pain control, thromboembolism prophylaxis, pressure injury monitoring, and early mobilization. The patient's Visual Analog Scale (VAS) pain score decreased from 7–9 during the first week to 1–3 by the fifth week. Mobilization progressed from complete bed dependence to short-distance ambulation. A pre-existing Stage 2 pressure injury progressed to Stage 3 postoperatively but improved to Stage 2 after appropriate wound care. Although complete independent ambulation was limited by neurological deficits and advanced age, functional improvement was achieved. This case highlights the importance of a multidisciplinary approach, close follow-up, and patient education in improving outcomes and facilitating early rehabilitation after complex revision hip arthroplasty.

papers.title: Accelerating Materials Discovery: A Review of Machine Learning in X‐Ray Absorption Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: X‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) is a critical technique for probing the local structural and electronic properties of materials. Advanced synchrotron radiation facilities generate complex, high‐dimensional spectra, which pose significant challenges for traditional analysis methods while simultaneously offering unprecedented opportunities for machine learning (ML). This review systematically elaborates how ML models are driving the transformation of XAS data analysis. We not only cover supervised and unsupervised learning methods for spectral classification and clustering but also delve into cutting‐edge deep learning architectures. These include graph neural networks for precise “structure‐to‐spectra” mapping and diffusion models for generative tasks and structure prediction. We provide a comprehensive overview of the key challenges in data‐driven XAS, including the feature engineering of spectra and structures, strategies for solving the “spectra‐to‐structure” Inverse Problem, and Sim2Real methods for bridging the “Domain Gap” between simulated and experimental data. Furthermore, we emphasize the importance of model eXplainable artificial intelligence and uncertainty quantification for building trust in scientific research. Finally, this review looks ahead to the future of the field, driven by materials informatics and autonomous experiments. Active Learning techniques, represented by Bayesian optimization, are pioneering “self‐driving” smart XAS experiments, which will greatly accelerate the discovery and design of new materials.

papers.title: Ready, Set, Learn! Energizing Workplace Training With Active Learning Principles
papers.abstract: Active learning is not simply about learning by doing. It incorporates diverse components to effectively cultivate and enhance trainees’ skills. However, existing research remains limited and sometimes contradictory regarding how adult learners prefer and apply these methods in workplace contexts, which calls for deeper investigation. This review explores active learning principles in workplace training and their effects on learning transfer and skill retention. Guided by Merrill’s Principles of Instruction (MPI), we analyzed 191 studies published between 2000 and 2025, as scholarship during this period reflects the field’s most substantive evolution, whereas earlier work is limited in scope and offers minimal insight into emerging trajectories. This body of literature was examined to address two guiding research questions: (a) What principles define active learning in workplace training? (b) How do these principles influence learning transfer and skill retention? Our analysis identified ten interconnected principles. They offering guidance for trainers, educators, and workplace learning designers who are striving to enhance training effectiveness through active learning.

papers.title: A Model for Developing Active Learning Teaching Skills among Thai Pre-service Teachers
papers.abstract: Active learning has become an essential instruction approach for preparing learners with the knowledge and skills required in the 21st century, and structured professional development can help pre-service teachers develop the competencies needed to implement such approaches effectively. The purpose of this study was to develop a model for enhancing active learning teaching skills among pre-service teachers. The study employed a research and development design consisting of three phases: model development, implementation, and evaluation. The implementation phase (Phase 2) was conducted over a 16-week semester during the pre-service teachers’ teaching practicum. The resulting model consisted of four major components: workshop training, lesson planning, coaching and feedback, and reflection and sharing activities. The findings revealed that the developed model demonstrated the highest levels of appropriateness (M = 4.90) and feasibility (M = 4.94). Furthermore, the pre-service teachers achieved lesson-planning and teaching-skill scores significantly higher than the established criterion of 80% (p < .05). The model was also evaluated positively across the instruction, institutional, and behavioral dimensions of Hammond’s framework. The study contributes to teacher education by providing an evidence-based model for developing active learning teaching competencies among pre-service teachers during their teaching practicum.

papers.title: Force-Electric Nanotentacles of Tantalum Implant Accelerate Cellular Energy Metabolism/Crosstalk for Immunomodulation-Vascularized Bone Integration.
papers.abstract: Current load-bearing bone implants primarily serve as static structural supports, still fall short of replicating the dynamic, spatiotemporal, and multifunctional coordination inherent in natural bone regeneration. Herein, we first develop a biomimetic force-electric responsive tantalum (Ta) implant with surface-nanostructured LiTaO3 (n- LiTaO3) via combining laser nanofabrication and Li+-induced in situ reaction, achieving favorable immunomodulation-mediated vascularized osseointegration under low-intensity pulsed ultrasound stimulation. The piezoelectric LiTaO3 nanotentacles convert ultrasound vibration into localized electrical signals, triggering Ca2 + influx, accelerating mitochondrial ATP production, and activating PI3K-AKT signaling pathway in BMSCs to promote osteogenesis. It also orchestrates a pro-osteoregenerative immune microenvironment through M2 macrophage polarization and immune-osteogenic crosstalk mediated by ECM-integrin-FAK axis. The force-electric response implant yet promotes angiogenesis mainly via enhancing intracellular Ca2 +-dependent eNOS/NO cue and cellular metabolism, reduces the inflammatory response in the dorsal subcutaneous tissue of rats, and further promotes vascularization and bone integration in femoral defects. The novel force-electric response Ta implant endows real-time controllable regulation of multifunctional tissue regeneration for using as patient-personalized load-bearing osteoarticular prostheses.

papers.title: Physics-Guided Decision-Support Framework for Melt Pool Prediction and Process Stability in Laser Powder Bed Fusion of Nitinol
papers.abstract: Powder bed fusion–laser beam (PBF-LB) of nickel–titanium (NiTi) has attracted increasing interest in aerospace, biomedical, and energy applications owing to its shape memory and superelastic properties, combined with the capability to fabricate complex geometries. However, the strong sensitivity of NiTi to thermal history and process variability makes predictive modeling and process parameter selection challenging. In this work, a physics-guided decision-support framework is developed for melt pool prediction and stability assessment during the PBF-LB processing of NiTi. A high-fidelity thermal finite element model incorporating CALPHAD-derived, temperature-dependent material properties was calibrated using a subset of experimental measurements and independently validated against additional experimental melt pool data. The calibrated model demonstrated good agreement with experiments, yielding mean absolute percentage errors of 4.22% and 5.63% for melt pool width and depth, respectively, on the validation dataset. A multi-output random forest surrogate trained on the validated simulation dataset enabled rapid prediction of melt pool geometric features, achieving test-set R2 values exceeding 0.95, together with low MAE and RMSE values, while five-fold cross-validation confirmed robust predictive performance. The proposed framework integrates surrogate predictions with physics-based melt pool stability criteria to rapidly identify physically feasible processing conditions, thereby providing a computationally efficient foundation for future supervisory process control strategies.

papers.title: Thermal and Mechanical Behaviors of Additively Manufactured Multilevel TPMS Metamaterials With Nonlinear Graded Infill
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures offer multifunctional potential. We propose a novel temperature‐guided multilevel TPMS design by infilling Diamond cells into an IWP framework with three spatial distributions. Ti6Al4V specimens were fabricated by laser powder bed fusion. Their transient thermal responses and room‐temperature quasi‐static compressive behaviors were evaluated separately through experiments and finite element simulations. These structures reduced top‐surface temperature by up to 80 °C versus primary IWP structures. In particular, the nonlinear graded configuration produced the lowest top‐surface temperature under the prescribed 300 s heating protocol, indicating delayed through‐thickness heat transfer. The separate thermal and mechanical assessments reveal a geometry‐mediated trade‐off between transient thermal‐shielding performance and compressive response. Although the temperature‐guided morphological heterogeneity reduces the elastic modulus, yield strength, and ultimate compressive strength, it disrupts coplanar stress concentration and promotes a more progressive 45° shear deformation mode, resulting in smoother post‐yield plateau responses. Therefore, the mechanical benefit of the multilevel configurations lies in their modified deformation mode and reduced stress oscillation rather than in improved overall load‐bearing strength or mechanical robustness. This study provides a field‐guided design strategy for load‐bearing and energy‐absorbing thermal‐protection lattices requiring delayed heat penetration and stable progressive deformation.

papers.title: A 3D-printed hydrogel scaffold promotes infected diabetic wound repair via anti-inflammation, angiogenesis, and extracellular matrix remodeling
papers.abstract: Infected diabetic wounds are difficult to heal due to bacterial colonization, persistent inflammation, impaired angiogenesis, and defective extracellular matrix remodeling. Conventional dressings and non-printed hydrogels often provide limited structural support, insufficient antibacterial protection, and inadequate wound microenvironment regulation. Here, we developed a multifunctional 3D-printed SilMA/HAMA dual-crosslinked hydrogel scaffold loaded with PDA-EGCG nanoparticles, termed SH-EGCG, for infected diabetic wound repair. The optimized bioink showed favorable printability, porous architecture, suitable mechanical properties, swelling behavior, and degradability. PDA-EGCG enabled sustained EGCG release and enhanced scaffold bioactivity. In vitro, SH-EGCG exhibited good hemocompatibility and cytocompatibility and showed antibacterial activity against methicillin-resistant S. aureus ( MRSA ) and Escherichia coli ( E. coli ). It also promoted L929 fibroblast proliferation and migration, enhanced HUVEC tube formation, and favored reparative M2 macrophage polarization. In vivo , SH-EGCG accelerated wound closure, reduced inflammatory infiltration and TNF-α expression, increased TGF-β and VEGF, and promoted granulation tissue formation, hair follicle regeneration, collagen deposition, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Transcriptomic analysis associated SH-EGCG treatment with re-epithelialization and extracellular matrix organization, including partial normalization of KRT17, KRT19, CDH1, COL1A1, and COL3A1 expression. These findings highlight SH-EGCG as a promising multifunctional scaffold for infected diabetic wound repair through antibacterial, immunomodulatory, pro-angiogenic, and extracellular matrix-remodeling effects.

papers.title: A Review on Advancing Stem Cell Therapy and Tissue Engineering to Regenerate Damaged Tissues and Organs
papers.abstract: In the field of regenerative medicine, developing stem cell therapy and tissue engineering has become a game-changing strategy that holds promise for replacing and repairing damaged organs and tissues. Innovative biological interventions are required since traditional therapy approaches frequently fail to restore total structural and functional integrity. A dynamic platform for tissue regeneration is offered by stem cell treatment, which is distinguished by the special qualities of self-renewal and differentiation. Simultaneously, tissue engineering creates functioning tissue structures that resemble natural biological systems by combining cells, biomaterials, and bioactive chemicals. Recent advances have considerably improved the efficacy of these approaches by using induced pluripotent stem cells, biomimetic scaffolds, and advanced fabrication techniques including three-dimensional bioprinting. Furthermore, the use of gene editing technologies, such as CRISPR-Cas9, has created new opportunities for precision medicine and tailored regenerative therapies. Despite these advancements, other challenges remain, including ethical problems, immunological rejection, tumorigenicity, and regulatory constraints. This review seeks to provide a complete overview of current developments in stem cell therapy and tissue engineering, emphasizing their complementary roles in regenerative medicine. It also examines recent technology advances, clinical uses, and current problems, as well as future prospects for developing safe, effective, and scalable regenerative therapies. Keywords: 3D Bioprinting, Tissue Engineering, Regenerative Medicine, Growth Factors, Biomedical Engineering, Organ Transplantation, Stem Cell.

papers.title: Effect of zinc-modified dental implants on osseointegration outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of preclinical animal studies
papers.abstract: Surface modification for dental implants has been generally studied to enhance osseointegration. Though, the beneficial effects of zinc-modified implants remain debatable depending on preclinical studies that present very different results. Consequently, the purpose of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to assess the effects of zinc-modified titanium implants on osseointegration. According to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, an electronic search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science to identify animal studies that evaluated the effect of zinc modified titanium implants on osseointegration. The included studies were evaluated based on the ratio of bone-to-implant contact (BIC), bone area (BA), and bone volume/total volume (BV/TV). Reporting quality was evaluated using ARRIVE 2.0 and the SYRCLE Risk of Bias tool, respectively. A total of 16 studies were identified and included in the review. Compared with zinc-free Ti implants, zinc-modified implants showed significantly greater BIC (Z = 3.89, P < 0.001), BA (Z = 8.40, P < 0.001), and BV/TV (Z = 5.43, P < 0.001). Although there was considerable heterogeneity, the overall effect consistently favored zinc-modified surfaces. Within the limitations of the available data from preclinical studies, implant surfaces modified with zinc were associated with improved histomorphometric indicators of osseointegration. However, there were significant methodological variations among the studies and lack of evidence of clinical relevance and hence a need for well-designed clinical studies.

papers.title: A hybrid grouping approach for high-dimensional multi-objective optimization of permanent magnet synchronous motors
papers.abstract: High-dimensional optimization of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) faces substantial challenges from complex nonlinear parameter couplings and the curse of dimensionality. This paper proposes a hybrid parameter grouping strategy that integrates Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS)-based global sensitivity analysis with partial correlation analysis. The method overcomes the initial-point dependency of traditional sensitivity approaches and preserves critical interdependencies among design parameters through a hierarchical two-stage procedure: sensitivity-based classification followed by correlation-based subdivision. The framework is implemented with Kriging surrogate modeling and NSGA-II optimization to enhance computational efficiency. Extensive finite element simulations on a V-type interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) validate the approach, demonstrating consistent performance improvements over conventional single-method grouping strategies. The theoretical superiority of the proposed method is also established through rigorous mathematical proofs.

summary_zh.method: 结合LHS全局灵敏度分析与偏相关分析，构建分层分组策略并耦合Kriging与NSGA-II。
summary_zh.result: 在V型内置式永磁电机上验证，性能优于传统单一分组方法。
summary_zh.validation: 基于有限元仿真的数值案例验证。

summary_en.motivation: High-dimensional optimization of permanent magnet synchronous motors is hindered by nonlinear parameter coupling and the curse of dimensionality.
summary_en.method: A hybrid grouping strategy combining LHS-based global sensitivity analysis with partial correlation analysis is coupled with Kriging surrogate modeling and NSGA-II optimization.
summary_en.result: The proposed hierarchical two-stage grouping consistently outperforms conventional single-method grouping strategies on a V-type IPMSM.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed through extensive finite element simulations of a specific motor design case.

papers.title: A Review on Advancing Stem Cell Therapy and Tissue Engineering to Regenerate Damaged Tissues and Organs
papers.abstract: In the field of regenerative medicine, developing stem cell therapy and tissue engineering has become a game-changing strategy that holds promise for replacing and repairing damaged organs and tissues. Innovative biological interventions are required since traditional therapy approaches frequently fail to restore total structural and functional integrity. A dynamic platform for tissue regeneration is offered by stem cell treatment, which is distinguished by the special qualities of self-renewal and differentiation. Simultaneously, tissue engineering creates functioning tissue structures that resemble natural biological systems by combining cells, biomaterials, and bioactive chemicals. Recent advances have considerably improved the efficacy of these approaches by using induced pluripotent stem cells, biomimetic scaffolds, and advanced fabrication techniques including three-dimensional bioprinting. Furthermore, the use of gene editing technologies, such as CRISPR-Cas9, has created new opportunities for precision medicine and tailored regenerative therapies. Despite these advancements, other challenges remain, including ethical problems, immunological rejection, tumorigenicity, and regulatory constraints. This review seeks to provide a complete overview of current developments in stem cell therapy and tissue engineering, emphasizing their complementary roles in regenerative medicine. It also examines recent technology advances, clinical uses, and current problems, as well as future prospects for developing safe, effective, and scalable regenerative therapies. Keywords: 3D Bioprinting, Tissue Engineering, Regenerative Medicine, Growth Factors, Biomedical Engineering, Organ Transplantation, Stem Cell.

llm.why_not_core: This review does not integrate AI/ML into any bioprinting workflow stage (pre/in/post-printing or digital twin) and provides no experimental validation or autonomous decision-making.

summary_zh.motivation: 传统疗法难以恢复受损组织器官的结构与功能完整性。
summary_zh.method: 综述干细胞治疗与组织工程的最新进展，涵盖iPSC、仿生支架、3D生物打印及CRISPR基因编辑。
summary_zh.result: 总结了互补性再生策略的临床潜力，并指出免疫排斥、致瘤性和监管等挑战。
summary_zh.validation: 文献综述，无实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: Conventional therapies often fail to restore the structural and functional integrity of damaged tissues and organs.
summary_en.method: This review surveys recent advances in stem cell therapy and tissue engineering, including iPSCs, biomimetic scaffolds, 3D bioprinting, and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing.
summary_en.result: It highlights the complementary roles of these strategies in regenerative medicine while identifying challenges such as immune rejection, tumorigenicity, and regulatory constraints.
summary_en.validation: Narrative literature review without experimental validation.

papers.title: A biomechanical optimized Zr 58 Cu 25 Al 14 Nb 3 bulk metallic glass dental implant improves peri‐implant stress distribution and bone quality under physiological loading
papers.abstract: Abstract While implant materials with bone‐mimetic elastic moduli are theoretically advantageous for reducing the stress shielding effect, the underlying mechanism remains incompletely understood, particularly in alveolar bone applications. In this study, we investigate the mechanism of excellent peri‐implant bone quality of a Zr 58 Cu 25 Al 14 Nb 3 bulk metallic glass (Nb3) dental implant in terms of its lower elastic modulus than commercial pure titanium (cpTi) and the stress distribution under masticatory mechanical loading. In vitro, Nb3 exhibited enhanced osteogenic potential over cpTi. In vivo, rat maxillary molar implants are subjected to a controllable cyclic loading program (10 N, 3 Hz, 0.12 s duration, 1800 cycles/day). The animal model coupled finite element analysis confirms that the lower elastic modulus of Nb3 implants promotes the more physiological stress distribution, and thus reduces stress concentration while increasing strain energy density in peri‐implant bone. Histomorphometry reveals that loaded Nb3 implants significantly accelerate mineral apposition rate, upregulate collagen III, and increase osteoblast density while reducing osteocyte number, demonstrating improved mechano‐adaptation. Transcriptomics identify coordinated upregulation of osteogenic, angiogenic, and mechanosensitive markers in Nb3‐loaded bone. Immunohistochemistry validates elevated expression of osteopontin and periostin, key mediators of mechanical signaling. These findings establish that Nb3's optimal elastic modulus enhances peri‐implant bone quality through biomechanical optimization of stress transfer that further activates mechanotransductive osteogenesis, providing a material‐based solution to stress shielding.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该研究关注牙种植体的应力遮挡与骨力学适应，与髋关节股骨柄应力遮挡机制在概念上相通，但解剖部位、载荷和植入物类型完全不同。
llm.why_not_core: It addresses dental alveolar bone and a bulk metallic glass dental implant, with no femoral stem geometry, no hip joint loading, no Gruen zone stress/strain quantification, and no micromotion or bone-implant interface contact modeling relevant to hip implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 低弹性模量植入物理论上可减轻应力遮挡，但其在牙槽骨中的力学机制尚不明确。
summary_zh.method: 采用Zr基块体金属玻璃牙种植体，结合体外细胞实验、大鼠上颌磨牙循环加载模型、有限元分析与组学检测。
summary_zh.result: 低模量Nb3种植体使种植体周围骨应力分布更接近生理状态，提高应变能密度并促进成骨与力学适应。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外细胞实验、大鼠在体循环加载实验及配套有限元分析进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: Bone-mimetic low-modulus implant materials are theoretically beneficial for mitigating stress shielding, yet the underlying mechanobiological mechanism in alveolar bone remains poorly defined.
summary_en.method: A Zr58Cu25Al14Nb3 bulk metallic glass dental implant was evaluated through in vitro osteogenic assays, a rat maxillary molar model with controlled cyclic loading, finite element analysis, histomorphometry, and transcriptomics.
summary_en.result: The lower modulus implant produced a more physiological peri-implant stress distribution, increased strain energy density, and enhanced mechanoadaptive osteogenesis compared with commercial pure titanium.
summary_en.validation: Findings were validated by combined in vitro cell experiments, in vivo rat cyclic loading experiments, and coupled finite element analysis.
